reuse.why: Every server, shared and client site, plus the new API field, calls the existing getScheduledAmount, and the approximate tolerance reuses getApproxNumberThreshold from shared/rules.

duplication.why: The five inlined midpoint ternaries and the template's hand copy are all removed; the rule exists only in getScheduledAmount.

placement.why: The rule sits in shared/schedules.ts and the API field is computed in the schedules-get handler with a dedicated list type; computing it there rather than in scheduleModel is acceptable but slightly ad hoc.

scope.why: Changes are confined to amount call sites, the helper, the API handler/type and tests; passing op at UI display sites is a necessary consequence of the rule, though useScheduleEdit's second call at line 153 is left without op.

maintainability.why: One function owns the whole rule with a clear comment and thorough tests; inserting op before the inverse boolean changes the positional signature, which is safe here only because no caller passed inverse.

bypasses_abstraction.where: No site keeps its own amount dispatch; all go through getScheduledAmount.

disguised_duplication.where: Copies were removed rather than reshaped.

abstraction_drift.where: getScheduledAmount gained one op parameter carrying the real variation (approximate vs exact); the isapprox branch is the rule itself, not a caller-specific special case, and no call site re-implements the logic.
